llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its SeaArt video-generation purpose, but it includes unsafe token-checking guidance that can print a password-equivalent SeaArt session token into logs.

dimensions.detail: The script reads only SEAART_TOKEN, sends requests to SeaArt endpoints, and does not read local files; the broad activation text for generic video requests could invoke an external service when the user did not explicitly name SeaArt.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses /update-config to persist SEAART_TOKEN locally and documents installing requests with pip; this is disclosed, but users should treat the persisted cookie as sensitive account access.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions tell the agent to check SEAART_TOKEN with echo $SEAART_TOKEN, which exposes the full session token in terminal output despite nearby guidance not to share tokens in logs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persisting a SeaArt session cookie is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but the unsafe echo instruction and session-token use create a material credential-handling risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Generating text-to-video and image-to-video through SeaArt is coherent with the skill purpose, and the external SeaArt endpoints and prompt/image data flows are disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. If used, do not run echo $SEAART_TOKEN; check token presence without printing it, keep the SeaArt cookie private, and understand that prompts, image URLs, and the token cookie are sent to seaart.ai.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the artifact explicitly instructs printing SEAART_TOKEN to check whether it is set, which can disclose the SeaArt session credential.
[T08] expected: Downgraded to a note: installing requests is expected for the Python script, though pinning dependencies would improve reproducibility.
[LP3] expected: Partially accepted as context: shell/Python/network/token use fits the stated function, but tighter declared permissions would make the sensitive token and network scope clearer.
[SQP-1] expected: Partially accepted as a scope note: generic video-generation trigger language is broad for a third-party authenticated service, but the SeaArt data flow is disclosed in the skill.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: hard-coded English locale headers are not ideal but do not materially change the security posture for this skill.
